record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space that is not isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Must X contain a subspace that fails the approximation property?

evidence.quote:
(Q.6). 1~ X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space which is not isomorphic to a
Hilbert space. Does X have a subspace which fails to have the AP ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Banach space $X$ is said to have the approximation property (AP) if for every compact subset $K \subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a bounded finite-rank linear operator $T : X \to X$ such that $\|Tx - x\| < \varepsilon$ for all $x \in K$. Equivalently, the identity operator on $X$ can be approximated uniformly on compact sets by finite-rank operators. A Banach space $X$ is said to have the hereditary approximation property if every closed (infinite-dimensional) subspace of $X$ has the approximation property.

Question: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space that is not isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Must $X$ contain a closed infinite-dimensional subspace that fails to have the approximation property?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is answered in the negative. Johnson and Szankowski (Annals of Mathematics, 2012, "Hereditary approximation property") constructed an infinite-dimensional Banach space, not isomorphic to a Hilbert space (in fact with a symmetric basis and not even asymptotically Hilbertian), all of whose closed infinite-dimensional subspaces have the approximation property. Thus there exist non-Hilbertian Banach spaces without any subspace failing AP.

status_evidence.title: Hereditary approximation property — Johnson and Szankowski, Annals of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Johnson and Szankowski constructed a Banach space with a symmetric basis, not isomorphic to ℓ2, all of whose subspaces have the approximation property (HAP).
status_evidence.claim: There exists a non-Hilbertian Banach space with the hereditary approximation property, so not every non-Hilbertian space has a subspace failing AP.

status_evidence.title: On hereditary approximation property — Anisca and Chlebovec
status_evidence.snippet: In 2010 Johnson and Szankowski constructed a HAP space with a symmetric basis but not isomorphic to ℓ2, hence not asymptotically Hilbertian.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the existence of non-Hilbertian HAP Banach spaces, resolving the question negatively.
